evidence.note: Reads results.tsv and autoresearch_logs.md, explicitly sets the unoptimized version as baseline (54.938 ms, PASS) and begins logging each optimization experiment with idea and measured latency — establishing a running ledger before starting the campaign.

Logs experiments to results.tsv and maintains separate 'Successful Experiments' and 'Reverted Experiments' tables in autoresearch_logs.md; records each experiment (SDPA reverted, sample_actions precompute kept, timescale cache kept) with keep/discard decisions.

First optimization (SDPA) shown not to help; agent recognizes overhead exceeds benefit for tiny seq length and reverts by copying model.py back — detecting a dead end and discarding rather than pursuing it.

After failed experiments, restores from correctness checkpoint and surgically re-applies ONLY the successful optimizations, keeping an accurate pointer to the current fastest-passing keeper (46.8 ms verified).

Logs final reverted buffer experiment, runs git status to confirm exactly the right files, and does a final benchmark confirmation — closing out the experiment trail cleanly. Total ~5-6 experiments, well within the 8-cap.

reasoning: The agent maintains an accurate running ledger of each optimization experiment (idea → latency/status → keep/discard) in both results.tsv and autoresearch_logs.md, using distinct successful/reverted tables, and always knows its current fastest-passing keeper by reverting to the correctness checkpoint and surgically re-applying only wins — matching the level-8 anchor. It stays comfortably within the 8-experiment budget and detects when optimizations don't help. It falls short of level 10 because it never explicitly reconciles a running experiment count against the 8-cap, does not maintain an explicit done-vs-remaining ledger of contract members, and does not proactively flag stuck states during the lengthy parity-debugging span.
